actions: Mapped campaigns file a room under its building, so two inns' kitchens keep their own memories and the GM is told the right one.
A place the GM names that the map lacks is added to the map beside the party; the GM may say where.
The map's additions are safer: an invented room never displaces a drawn one, and each refusal says why.
A room named through an invented building gets one place on the map, and a tap inside an added building no longer removes it.
An invented building without a trade word is drawn larger when a room the story names will not fit.
A room re-stated inside an invented building keeps its one place; a room named through a square finds its inn.
A pair the GM writes under a building it just invented is that building's room; a place put on a landmark draws no rooms.
Dice gain larger classic dots, optional Large Numbers, and a Teal Glass preset with consistent preset names.
Going Down pauses longer at the top, and metal dice regain gentle recessed numbers and dots.
During character creation the progress bar also jumps ahead to any step already reached, after a change made on an earlier one.
In character creation, a subrace or lineage card's granted spells and abilities open their reference cards on a click.
The map draws a campaign's starting place as the story describes it: open country, a sized settlement, or a place inside a named town.
None and Fade dismiss all dice together; other exit animations retain their stagger.
Starting places land on the map as the story tells it: a wreck ashore, a dungeon at a real cave, a tavern in town.
The New game confirmation follows the light scheme.
The map lives in the side drawer's Map tab with wheel zoom and drag pan; an enlarge button opens it full screen.
The map's title, compass and scale bar stay put while you pan and zoom, and the scale follows the zoom.
On a map card, "We are here" is now "Current location".
The drawer map is the map alone: round buttons to enlarge and to find the party, and it remembers your zoom after full screen.
The map opens close on the party and always fills its panel; dragging it off the edge is no longer possible.
Pulling the drawer wider reveals more map without moving it, and full screen keeps the drawer's view.
The map buttons sit together bottom right, the party's dagger looks like the one on the map, and cards sit above them.
Panning and zooming the map no longer shows a blank strip before it draws in.
The map's title plaque shows the party's location trail; tap a tier to go up a level.
Map cards offer Add note: your own words on a place, kept with the campaign. Current location is gone.
The dice table opens empty, with Bone for new users and saved appearance choices retained.
Sketch and Ink Sketch dice add continuous pencil hatching, ink-colored profile edges and hatched moving shadows.
Sketch dice use bounded hatching on Scurry legs; failed graphics startup offers recovery and keeps saved looks.
Going up a level from the map's location trail opens close on the party, as every sheet does, instead of the whole sheet.
New players' dice start as Sketch and leave with Fade; a look or exit you already chose stays yours.

Map library 0.13.0: roads and rivers now meet across the edges of open-country sheets, so those sheets are redrawn in mapped campaigns.
Tapping water on the realm map now says the point lies in the sea or a lake; coastal land can be stood on.
Dice Simulator 0.97.0 adds installed-font browsing and personal font-file imports; unavailable number fonts use the system font.
In a mapped campaign, the Game Master is now told where you placed the party with We are here.
Remove Melt from dice exit options and random selections, with safe fallbacks for previously saved choices.
Replace expanding holes with a smooth fade after melting dice flow into one puddle.
Fade the puddle and its shadow together.
Melting dice flow into one smooth, continuous puddle before dissolving.
Correct release checksums across Windows and Linux checkouts.

Remove separate blob rims and keep the liquid outline smooth.
Add Melt: dice soften into glossy puddles, stretch into goo, and disappear through expanding holes.
Prepare melting shadows during loading to prevent a cold animation pause.
Bug reports now include the signed-in reporter’s username in email notifications and the bug tracker.
Reports from several players retain each reporter’s name when combined during bug sync.
The die you are asked to roll now waits ready at the bottom of the story; Roll throws it from where it lies.
Hold back, or the car screen, takes the waiting die away quietly.
Made the roll a modal: when the Game Master asks for a check, the die and Hold back are the only ways on.
A reload or leaving Car Mode brings a waiting roll back; nothing can be typed past it.
Added editable invitation subjects and messages with a full email preview before sending.
Changed Resend to open the saved message for editing and review before delivery.
Kept secure invitation links and access instructions in the preview and outgoing email.
Added Gmail invitations with Google sign-in, single-use links and automatic approval on acceptance.
Added seven-day invitation expiry, resend and revoke controls, and persistent email delivery receipts.
Preserved existing active access when accepting an invitation.
Grouped player activity into collapsible panels with new request counts since the operator’s previous visit.
Added production release history with dated, concise action notes.
Added recipient previews and direct beta email sending with persistent delivery receipts.
Reorganized Settings into focused groups.
Kept every menu item reachable on short phone and desktop screens.
Moved Player rolls own dice beside Dice appearance in Settings.
Retired the obsolete in-band action button setting.
Updated the dice roller with pointer-aligned dragging, double-click rerolls, and spinning tosses.
Renamed the Assassin feature to Inevitability throughout its class reference.
Preloaded the live dice rendering pipeline to reduce the first roll delay.
